method.method_draft: Use geometric decomposition into a trapezoid and an equilateral triangle. From the diagram, split the pentagon along segment EC into lower quadrilateral ABCE and upper triangle CDE. From the text, EA=AB=BC=2 and angles A and B are 120 degrees. The slanted sides AE and BC each have vertical height component 2 sin 60°=sqrt(3) and horizontal outward component 2 cos 60°=1, so E and C lie on a line parallel to AB at height sqrt(3). Thus EC=1+AB+1=4. Therefore ABCE is a trapezoid with bases AB=2 and EC=4 and height sqrt(3), so its area is ((2+4)/2)sqrt(3)=3sqrt(3). Since CD=DE=4 and EC=4, triangle CDE is equilateral with side 4, so its area is (sqrt(3)/4)16=4sqrt(3). Add the two areas to get 7sqrt(3).
